ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontally placed square, and another square is rotated into a diamond shape. The two squares share the lower-right vertex of the horizontal square, and one side of the rotated square is along the diagonal direction of the horizontal square from lower right to upper left. The shaded overlapping part is a quadrilateral. Reasoning: According to the specified coordinate method, let the horizontal unit square be 0<=x<=1, 0<=y<=1, and the common vertex be V=(1,0). Take the direction of one side of the rotated square as u=(-1/√2, 1/√2), and the direction of the other adjacent side as v=(1/√2, 1/√2). Therefore the relevant vertices of the rotated square are P=V+u=(1-1/√2, 1/√2), T=V+u+v=(1,√2). The vertices of the overlapping region in order are V, P, Q, R, where R=(1,1), and Q is the intersection point of side PT and the upper side y=1 of the horizontal square. The direction of side PT is v, so starting from P there is (x,y)=(1-1/√2,1/√2)+t(1/√2,1/√2). Let y=1, obtain t=√2-1, therefore x=2-√2, so Q=(2-√2,1). For quadrilateral V=(1,0), P=(1-1/√2,1/√2), Q=(2-√2,1), R=(1,1), use the shoelace formula. Let a=1/√2, then the points are V=(1,0), P=(1-a,a), Q=(2-2a,1), R=(1,1). The forward sum of the shoelace is 1·a+(1-a)·1+(2-2a)·1+1·0=3-2a; the reverse sum is 0·(1-a)+a(2-2a)+1·1+1·1=1+2a. The area is |(3-2a)-(1+2a)|/2=(4a-2)/2=2a-1=√2-1.

raw_record.question_text: Two squares with side 1 have a common vertex, and the edge of one of them lies along the diagonal of the other. What is the area of the overlap between the squares?

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate polygon calculation. Read the figure as an upright unit square with the common vertex at its lower-right corner and the second unit square tilted so one of its sides follows the upright square's diagonal direction. Place the upright square at 0<=x<=1, 0<=y<=1 with common vertex V=(1,0). The tilted square has side vectors u=(-1/sqrt(2),1/sqrt(2)) along the diagonal direction and v=(1/sqrt(2),1/sqrt(2)). Its relevant vertices are V, P=V+u=(1-1/sqrt(2),1/sqrt(2)), and T=V+u+v=(1,sqrt(2)). The overlap polygon is V -> P -> Q -> R, where R=(1,1) and Q is the intersection of the tilted square side PT with the top edge y=1 of the upright square. Solving gives Q=(2-sqrt(2),1). Apply the shoelace formula to V, P, Q, R, or equivalently split the polygon into simple triangles/trapezoids, to obtain area sqrt(2)-1.

推理：按指定坐标法，令水平单位正方形为 0<=x<=1, 0<=y<=1，共同顶点为 V=(1,0)。旋转正方形的一条边方向取 u=(-1/√2, 1/√2)，另一条相邻边方向取 v=(1/√2, 1/√2)。因此旋转正方形相关顶点为 P=V+u=(1-1/√2, 1/√2)，T=V+u+v=(1,√2)。重叠区域顶点依次为 V, P, Q, R，其中 R=(1,1)，Q 是边 PT 与水平正方形上边 y=1 的交点。边 PT 方向为 v，所以从 P 出发有 (x,y)=(1-1/√2,1/√2)+t(1/√2,1/√2)。令 y=1，得 t=√2-1，因此 x=2-√2，所以 Q=(2-√2,1)。

method.method_draft: Use a geometric dissection of the tilted square. From the figure, focus on the half of the tilted square lying inside/left of its vertical diagonal through the common vertex and top vertex. This half is a right isosceles triangle whose area is half the area of the unit tilted square, namely 1/2. The upright square cuts off only the small top cap above its top side. Since the diagonal of a unit square has length sqrt(2), the top vertex of the tilted square is sqrt(2) units above the common vertex, while the upright square's top side is 1 unit above it. Thus the cap has vertical leg sqrt(2)-1. Because the tilted square sides make 45-degree lines, the cap is also a right isosceles triangle with both legs sqrt(2)-1. Its area is ((sqrt(2)-1)^2)/2. Subtract this cap from 1/2 to get 1/2 - ((sqrt(2)-1)^2)/2 = sqrt(2)-1.

The two squares share the lower-right vertex of the horizontal square, and one side of the rotated square is along the diagonal direction of the horizontal square from lower right to upper left. The shaded overlapping part is a quadrilateral.

Reasoning: According to the specified coordinate method, let the horizontal unit square be 0<=x<=1, 0<=y<=1, and the common vertex be V=(1,0). Take the direction of one side of the rotated square as u=(-1/√2, 1/√2), and the direction of the other adjacent side as v=(1/√2, 1/√2). Therefore the relevant vertices of the rotated square are P=V+u=(1-1/√2, 1/√2), T=V+u+v=(1,√2). The vertices of the overlapping region in order are V, P, Q, R, where R=(1,1), and Q is the intersection point of side PT and the upper side y=1 of the horizontal square. The direction of side PT is v, so starting from P there is (x,y)=(1-1/√2,1/√2)+t(1/√2,1/√2). Let y=1, obtain t=√2-1, therefore x=2-√2, so Q=(2-√2,1).

For quadrilateral V=(1,0), P=(1-1/√2,1/√2), Q=(2-√2,1), R=(1,1), use the shoelace formula. Let a=1/√2, then the points are V=(1,0), P=(1-a,a), Q=(2-2a,1), R=(1,1). The forward sum of the shoelace is 1·a+(1-a)·1+(2-2a)·1+1·0=3-2a; the reverse sum is 0·(1-a)+a(2-2a)+1·1+1·1=1+2a. The area is |(3-2a)-(1+2a)|/2=(4a-2)/2=2a-1=√2-1.
